diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the positive constants $C_{tr}$ and $C_{inv}$ depend only on the regularity of the mesh and the polynomial degree $l$ of the finite element space

issues.failure_explanation: The continuous trace theorem of Evans on a fixed domain has a constant depending on the domain; applied to each element K the constant scales with h_K and is not uniform in the mesh as claimed. The inverse inequality for polynomials reads ||w||_{1,K}^2 <= C h_K^{-2}||w||_{0,K}^2, not h_K^{-1}. Neither cited result, as invoked, gives the stated intermediate inequalities; the final bound ||w||_{0,∂K}^2 <= C h_K^{-1}||w||_{0,K}^2 is true only as a separate standard discrete trace inequality, not as the composition written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two-step argument by the standard discrete trace inequality ||w||_{0,∂K}^2 <= C h_K^{-1} ||w||_{0,K}^2 for w in P^l(K) on shape-regular meshes (proved by scaling), and define \tilde C accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the constant \tilde C used in the boundedness and stability lemmas (and hence the penalty threshold on η) is invalid as written; the conclusions remain true via the standard scaled discrete trace inequality.
issues.title: Discrete trace bound derived from misstated trace theorem and inverse inequality
issues.why_classification: A local citation/derivation fix with a standard inequality; all conclusions, rates and scope survive.

issues.failure_explanation: On an interior face |{q}|^2 <= (|q_1|^2+|q_2|^2)/2, which yields the factor 1/2, but on a boundary face {q}=q|_K, so the face contributes ∫_f h_K|q_K|^2 to the left side while only (1/2)∫_f h_K|q_K|^2 to the right side. The inequality is false whenever the boundary-face contribution is nonnegligible; the correct factor is 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the factor 1/2 by 1 (or bound interior and boundary faces separately), and adjust the constant (2η)^{-1/2} to η^{-1/2} and the threshold on η accordingly in Lemmas 2–3 and all statements quoting it.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants μ_0^{-1}(2η)^{-1/2}\tilde C in Lemma 2 and 3, and therefore the explicit penalty threshold η > max{1,μ_1^2}\tilde C^2/(2μ_0^2) used throughout, are off by a factor 2; qualitative boundedness/stability for sufficiently large η is unaffected.
issues.title: Factor 1/2 in face-to-element bound fails on boundary faces
issues.why_classification: Only an explicit constant/threshold changes; all results hold with the corrected constant after a routine local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then for any $\fb\in \Vb^*$, the problem \eqref{eqn1.18} has a unique solution $\Eb_h\in\Vb_h$

issues.failure_explanation: V_h is not contained in V=H_0(curl,Ω), so for a general f ∈ V* the pairing ⟨f,v_h⟩ in scheme (eqn1.18) is undefined, and ||E_h||_{curl,Ω} does not exist for discontinuous E_h (its global curl is not in L^2). The bound ⟨f,E_h⟩ ≤ ||f||_{V*}||E_h||_h is therefore unsupported. The scheme is only meaningful when \tilde l ∈ L^2(Ω) (so ⟨f,v_h⟩=∫\tilde l·v_h), which is implicitly used in the derivation but never assumed; \tilde l contains ∇×(\tilde μ^{-1}B^{n-1}), which need not be in L^2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume \tilde l ∈ L^2(Ω) (i.e. f represented by an L^2 function), define ⟨f,v_h⟩=∫\tilde l·v_h on V(h), replace ||f||_{V*} by ||\tilde l||_{0,Ω} and ||E_h||_{curl} by ||E_h||_{0,Ω} in the bound, and restrict Theorem 3 to such f.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform bound, the existence/uniqueness theorem's quantifier 'for any f ∈ V*', and the error estimate (which uses uniform boundedness) are stated for data on which the scheme is not defined.
issues.title: Right-hand side f ∈ V* is not defined on the nonconforming DG space; bound via ||E_h||_curl invalid
issues.why_classification: A standard extra assumption on the data and a one-line change in the estimate preserve all conclusions and rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, if $\Eb \in \Hb_0(\curlb; \Omega) \cap \Hb^{s+1}(\Omega)$ for some number $s > 0$, then
Applying the error bounds \eqref{energy norm estimate} and \eqref{eqn:lemma4-3}, we derive from \eqref{eqn:error bound} that
if $\Eb\in\Hb_0(\curlb;\Omega)\cap\Hb^{3/2}(\Omega)$ and $\nabla\times \Eb \in \Hb^1(\Omega)$, we have the optimal linear convergence order

issues.failure_explanation: The dominant term in (eqn:error bound) is (C_{Eb}+C_{Ehb})||E−E_I||_{0,Ω}, which enters linearly, so ||E_I−E_h||_h^2 ≲ ||E−E_I||_{0,Ω}. To obtain ||E−E_I||_{0,Ω} ≤ C h^{min{s,l}+1}, estimate (eqn:lemma4-3) requires E ∈ H^{s+1}(Ω). The theorem only assumes E ∈ H^{s+1/2}(Ω), under which (eqn:lemma4-3) yields h^{min{s−1/2,l}+1}, giving ||E−E_h||_h ≤ C h^{(min{s−1/2,l}+1)/2}, a quarter order less than claimed. In particular for l=1 with E ∈ H^{3/2}, the argument gives only O(h^{3/4}), not the advertised O(h).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either strengthen the hypothesis to E ∈ H_0(curl;Ω) ∩ H^{s+1}(Ω) (keeping the rate h^{(min{s,l}+1)/2} and requiring H^2 for optimal linear order), or keep H^{s+1/2} and weaken the conclusion to h^{(min{s−1/2,l}+1)/2}.
issues.overall_effect: The stated rate (error_bd) and the subsequent 'optimal linear convergence' remark under H^{3/2} regularity are unproved; the numerical-example claim of matching Theorem 4 rests on this.
issues.title: Error estimate rate not supported by the assumed regularity H^{s+1/2}
issues.why_classification: Result survives in comparable form, but either the regularity scope must be strengthened by half a derivative or the rate weakened; the advertised optimal-order regime is narrowed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Eb$ and $\Eb_h$ be the solutions of \eqref{eqn1.1} and \eqref{eqn1.18}, respectively.

Assume \eqref{eqn1.other}, $m<\epsilon_0$ and $\eta > \max\{1,\mu_1^2\}\,\tilde{C}^2/(2\,\mu_0^2)$. If $\Eb_h\in \Vb_h$ is a solution of the problem \eqref{eqn1.18}, then $\|\Eb_h\|_h$ is uniformly bounded

issues.failure_explanation: The statement of Theorem 4 assumes only mesh regularity, solution regularity and the penalty condition, but the proof invokes m < ε_0 to absorb the (1+ε)m||E_I−E_h||^2 term, uses Lemma 4 (uniform boundedness, which requires m < ε_0) to define C_{Ehb}, and presupposes existence/uniqueness of E_h (Theorem 3, which requires m < ε_0). Without m < ε_0 the discrete problem may fail to have a solution and the absorption step fails.

failure_location.quote: Since $m<\epsilon_0$, we can choose a sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses (eqn1.other) and m < ε_0 to the statement of Theorem 4.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the error estimate is not established for the regime m ≥ ε_0; it is only proved under the smallness condition used elsewhere.
issues.title: Theorem 4 omits the hypothesis m < ε_0 used in its proof
issues.why_classification: Adding the standing smallness condition already required for existence is a routine local repair preserving the result.
